News Items 
Culture Night Kildare  
Culture Night took place on 19 September and saw almost 70 events across Kildare 
(see pages 14/15). 
 
Strategic Projects and Public Realm - Emily Square 
Minister Martin Heydon officially opened Emily Square on Friday 12 September.  The 
launch event was very successful with music provided on the Square by local 
musicians (see page 20). 
 
Brigid, Spirit of Kildare 2026 Programme 
Planning has commenced for the Brigid, Spirit of Kildare Festival 2026. This festival 
is set to take place across the county over the February bank holiday weekend and 
will place an emphasis on the County of Kildare and the achievements and talent 
within the county (see page 50). 
 
Local Economic and Community Plan (LECP) 
Work continues with the online LECP monitoring tool developed using Microsoft 
Lists. A progress report will be prepared at the end of 2025 (see page 52). 
 
Entente Florale 2025 
Maynooth was awarded gold standard in the 2025 Entente Florale competition at the 
prize giving in Velenje, Slovenia on 27 September (see pages 61/62). 
 
Irish Planning Institute (IPI) Planning Awards 2025 
Kildare County Council received two National Awards and a Highly Commended 
Recognition (see page 70) 
 
Kildare Fáilte 
For the second year running, Into Kildare, in partnership with Kildare County Council, 
supported the AMGEN Irish Golf Open at The K Club from 04 to 08 September (see 
page 78).

Diary/Calendar 
Kildare Biodiversity Conference 2025 
Kildare County Council, in partnership with Kildare Wildlife Rescue, announced the 
return of the Kildare Biodiversity Conference.  This exciting event will take place on 
the 18 and 19 October in the Keadeen Hotel, Newbridge (see page 8). 
 
Polling Day – Presidential Election 
Presidential Elections Polling Day is 24 October 2025 (see page 9). 
 
The Creative Path 
The Creative Path is an art therapy programme for people living with an acquired 
brain injury. The programme will commence on Monday, 06 October and run for six 
weeks. (see page 13). 
 
Budget 2026 
Statutory Budget meeting agreed for Monday, 17 November 2025 at 3.00p.m.   
Budget briefing agreed for Monday 10 November 2025 at 3.00p.m. (see page 19). 
 
Shackleton Experience  
The museum was handed over to Kildare County Council/Athy Heritage Company on 
the 01 October and will formally open on Friday, 10 October (see page 21). 
 
Climate Week:  
The Climate Action Office is preparing to hold Climate Week during 28-31 October.  
A Halloween costume pop up event will take place the week commencing the 20 
October to get everyone in the Halloween spirit (see page 60). 
 
Upgrade to Naas Farmers Market  
KFM radio will be delivering an outside broadcast at Naas Farmer’s Market on 01 
November to promote the market and highlight the additional investment secured 
through the Department of Agriculture, Food and Marine as part of the Flavours of 
Kildare initiative (see page 82).

Greenway (Maynooth to Leixlip)

Council hosted Minister for Climate, 
Environment and Energy and Minister 
for Transport, Darragh O’Brien and 
Minister for Further and Higher 
Education, Research, Innovation and 
Science, James Lawless in the

Leixlip.  The official opening marks the 
completion of 7.75km section of the 
Royal Canal Greenway, extending 
from Maynooth Harbour to 
Confey/Cope Bridge, Leixlip.

News and Highlights – Library  
 
“We may sit in our library and yet 
be in all quarters of the earth.” ― 
John Lubbock, The Pleasures of 
Life 
 
Kildare Library Service staffed a stand 
outside the canteen in Áras on Friday 
26 September to create Awareness of 
National Public Libraries Open Day, 
Kildare Reader’s Festival and library 
programming in general. 
Bilingual freestyle skipping, chemistry 
workshops and clothes alterations 
were just some of the extraordinary 
events held across Kildare Libraries on 
Saturday 27 September for National 
Public Libraries Open Day. Kildare 
Library Service has said goodbye to 
Jacqui McCabe after many years’ 
services in Clane Library and we 
welcome Aidan Gough, our new 
Mobile Library and van driver. The 
Mobile service will resume on 30 
September and Clane Library hours 
have been extended. 
 
Culture Night 
Kildare Library Service hosted a range 
of events from Drumming Workshops 
to Celebrating Irish Language and 
Gaelic Culture. There was music on 
the steps of Naas Library and Cultural 
Centre with performances in the 
chamber later and an opportunity to 
learn some sean-nós dancing steps 
while award winning sean-nós singer 
Féilim MacDonncha taught the 
audience traditional Irish songs.  
‘Soundings’ in Athy with David Walsh 
brought people back to the popular 
literature of their school days. All 
events were well attended.

Global Goals Class Sets 
To celebrate Sustainable Development 
Goals (SDG) week 2025, Kildare 
Libraries launched our Global Goals 
class sets in partnership with Green-
Schools. The collection, which is 
available to borrow through our 
libraries, features a diverse selection 
of children’s books, each chosen to 
reflect and explore one or more of the 
17 United Nations Global Goals for 
Sustainable Development. The aim is 
to introduce primary school students to 
important global issues through 
accessible and inspiring stories. Each 
book is supported by tailor-made 
resources and worksheets, designed 
to deepen understanding and spark 
classroom discussion.

Health Awareness 
Chair yoga classes are ongoing in 
Athy and Kildare Town with yoga in the 
Men’s and Women’s shed in Naas. 
Naas held talks on Mindful Running 
while Breathwork workshops were held 
in Naas and Maynooth. Newbridge 
held a talk on dietary advice for people 
on GLP-1 medication.

Athy, Kildare and Newbridge libraries 
hosted talks on seed saving in 
September. Numerous crafting groups 
in libraries explored making and

basic sewing and mending alterations 
workshop with Fiona Breslin. 
 
Library Digital Services 
Support for mobile wallets has been 
added to the Kildare Library app, 
allowing members to save their library 
card to Apple or Google Wallet with a 
single tap. This enhancement makes 
access faster and more convenient; 
users can present their card instantly 
from their phone’s wallet, even offline, 
without opening the library app. The 
change is designed to streamline 
borrowing, reduce delays at service

The Creative Path 
The Creative Path is an art therapy 
programme for people living with an 
acquired brain injury. The programme 
is in partnership with Creative Ireland, 
Kildare Library and Arts Service, 
Headway (acquired brain injury) and 
Platinum Clubhouse (mental health 
recovery). The aim of this programme 
is to support and nurture mental health 
and wellbeing through art therapy 
where everyone’s recovery can be 
encouraged and empowered through 
creativity. 
The programme was launched on 
Thursday, 25 September in Newbridge 
Library. The programme will 
commence on Monday 06 October and 
run for six weeks. (One Monday 
session per week). 
 
Kildare County Archives and Local 
Studies 
The annual John Devoy 
Commemoration took place in Naas 
Library and Cultural Centre on 25 
September. Devoy’s chair was on 
display for the first time, donated to 
Kildare County Council’s County 
Archives by Frank MacGabhann 
whose aunts, Alice Cumiskey and Lily 
Carragher, looked after John Devoy in 
his final years in the U.S. Speakers 
included the Cathaoirleach of Kildare 
County Council, Councillor Carmel 
Kelly, Mayor of Naas, Councillor 
Seamie Moore, Director of Services, 
Joe Boland and Frank MacGabhann. 
The event also included a screening of 
the documentary, John Devoy: the 
Greatest of the Fenians, by local film 
maker, Donal Higgins. 
 
Nine working drawings of the 
alterations to the Naas Town Hall and 
proposed Free Library from 1903, 
which were returned to Naas UDC in 
1993 by the daughter of a former town 
surveyor has been added to the Online 
Archives here. A recording of the 1993 
presentation at a meeting of the UDC 
has also been made available by kind 
permission of Gerry McCarthy, Naas 
Local History Group.

Farm Dispatches – Athy and Naas 
Farm Dispatches, a participatory 
dance/arts project involving different 
adult communities in Athy and Naas 
districts and professional dance-
theatre artists and writers, led by 
choreographer Philippa Donnellan with 
poet/academic Catherine Gander and 
dancers Sarah Ryan and Ben Sullivan, 
invited people to connect and 
creatively explore themes surrounding 
farming life and our fractured 
relationship with nature through dance 
and poetry, conversation and 
performance. The project ran from 25 
August to 04 October 2025 including a 
series of lively dance and poetry 
workshops with Athy group the Willow 
Weavers.  
 
From Ganger’s Hut to House of 
Memories - Rathangan 
A programme of activities organised by 
Creative Rathangan Meitheal involves 
gathering twenty oral histories, and a 
range of associated 
memorabilia, capturing the socio-
economic impact of Bord na Mona on 
Rathangan.  A replica Ganger’s Hut – 
has been built as part of the project - 
repurposing a workspace as a 
museum/display area. A workshop 
focussing on Richard Griffiths work for 
the Bog Commissioners in mapping 
the Bog of Allen took place on 27 
September. A Quaker Trail for families 
new to the area and interested in 
Quaker History took place on 28 
September.

Key Activities  
For the second year running, Into 
Kildare, in partnership with Kildare 
County Council, supported the 
AMGEN Irish Golf Open at The K Club 
from 04–08 September. 
Into Kildare hosted a promotional 
stand across all four days of the 
tournament, supported by ten tourism 
and hospitality businesses from across 
the county. Each participating 
business generously contributed prizes 
for the “Spin the Wheel” activation, 
which proved very popular with 
visitors. Over 80,000 spectators 
attended the event, providing an 
excellent platform to promote Kildare. 
Festival-branded Taste of Kildare lawn 
chairs were placed on the Kildare 
Lawn, offering attendees a place to 
relax, while two local food trucks, 
Hartes of Kildare and Donadea 
Wagyu, showcased the county’s food 
offering with delicious dishes. 
Throughout the week, Chief Executive 
Áine Mangan also hosted and 
entertained a number of tourism 
industry guests, strengthening 
connections and highlighting the best 
of what Kildare has to offer. 
Aine Mangan, Eoghan Corry and Into Kildare

Meeting of the year at Naas 
Racecourse.  
Into Kildare hosted a press trip through 
TBEX, welcoming two international 
content creators from the US and 
Canada from 14–16 September. 
The trip focused on Kildare Town and 
Athy, with accommodation provided by 
the Silken Thomas Hotel and the 
Clanard Court Hotel. Highlights 
included a visit to the Irish National 
Stud, a VR experience at Kildare Town 
Heritage Centre, an exclusive preview 
of the Shackleton Experience, a barge 
trip, and dining in local restaurants. 
The content creators shared their 
experiences across their digital 
channels, generating valuable 
international content and positioning 
Kildare as a premier tourism 
destination.

development. The project remains on 
track, and further updates will be 
shared via www.repowerregions.eu.
